chapter: Funeral customs, Pickwick band and later years
title: The Pickwick band and the Douroux family
summary: Love recalls musicians in the old Pickwick band, including Dominguez and old man DeRooks, and the nephews of Dolly who play modern jazz.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: What ever happened to them? Did they have a Pickwick band here?
Oh, that was a long time before my time. My father was a young man then. He used to come down here. I'll tell you some fellas was playing in that band. The country.

The old man. The old man. They come from Mombardo first there somewhere. Yeah. Well, Deconjay and, let me see who else was in that band. Deconjay. I believe old man Dominguez, the bass player, was in that band. Paul Dominguez daddy. He's a bass violin and a bass player, too. He was one of the best bands in the city. DeRooks was in that, too. Old man DeRooks. The boy's father. Old man DeRooks. He was a great company player. I don't know the boys. What are their names? I don't know them boys. They play music? They play music? Dolly got a bunch of little nephews. They play music now? Dolly got a bunch of little nephews. Oh. Yeah. They play modern jazz. Yeah. They play swell. I don't know the boys. What are their names? I don't know them boys.
Oh yeah, Dolly got a bunch of little nephews.
